candidates.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
candidates.reason: Agentic workloads materially change serving-system bottlenecks, state lifetime, resource affinity, and caching opportunities. The paper includes production traces and concrete serving design explorations, so it is directly relevant to inference-system architecture rather than only application benchmarking.
evidence: Ten representative agentic applications with unified systems-level instrumentation
Reports non-LLM components dominating latency in 5/10 applications and sandbox working sets up to 28 GB per session
Design explorations report 29–40% latency reduction from task-aware serving, up to 4.5x from communication-aware placement, and 4.6x memory reduction from state offloading

candidates.title: Potential Applications of HBF in LLM Serving Systems
candidates.reason: Examines High-Bandwidth Flash as an additional serving-memory tier for MoE expert residency and multi-model serving. It directly targets capacity pressure in model-state residency and is relevant to SSD/flash-aware inference-system design.
evidence: Models HBF as a capacity-oriented extension to HBM while preserving the HBM-resident execution path
Evaluates MoE serving via increased expert replication and multi-model serving via reduced model loading/hot-model replication
Results are simulation-based, so a later formal audit should verify assumptions and distinguish projected benefits from measured hardware performance
